business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal system grounded in the Napoleonic Code tradition; strong EU-law integration in commercial and AML/CFT matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (BIT, signed 2007)
France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA, signed 26 November 2013; effective 1 January 2015)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; not yet in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT and UBO register obligations: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-60 and R.561-1 to R.561-41 of the French Code monétaire et financier, as amended by Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 13 October 2016, Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Décret n° 2020-1062 of 3 August 2020 (transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directives (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Loi Sapin II) establishing the French beneficial-owner register; Articles L.561-45 to L.561-57 and R.561-19 to R.561-25 Code monétaire et financier governing the déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif filed with the RCS/Greffe; Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-166-1 on registered-office and filing requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current registry extract of each corporate shareholder (K-bis equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (for PRC shareholders: State Administration for Market Regulation-derived certificate; for Hong Kong: Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC accession effective 7 November 2023; apostille issued by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its authorized provincial offices) plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (pouvoir) granted by the corporate shareholder to the French incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative or board of directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passports or national identity documents of each ultimate beneficial owner, legal representative, and administrator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the issuing state, plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for the planned share-capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing bank is overseas, plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (attestation de bonne situation) of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the shareholder's registered-office jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and on at least a rolling 12-month basis of all shareholders, managers, and UBOs against (1) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (2) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, including Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) 2580/2001; (3) French national asset-freeze arrêtés issued by the Direction générale du Trésor; (4) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, given USD-clearing via retainer wire and Wise B2B payment rails; and (5) PEP databases covering French, EU, and foreign politically exposed positions per Article R.561-18 of the Code monétaire et financier. All screening results, negative media hits, and red flags must be documented in the AML/CFT compliance file; any reasonable suspicion triggers the mandatory déclaration de soupçon to TRACFIN.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability verified via the INPI national company-data repository (data.inpi.fr) and the RCS database of the Greffes des tribunaux de commerce (Infogreffe)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings and corporate instruments must be in French (Loi n° 94-665, Loi Toubon). The dénomination sociale must be in Latin script; a foreign-language name requires a registered French transliteration and a French version for all commercial documentation. The name must be distinguishable from pre-existing RCS entries and protected trademarks and must not mislead the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The INPI attestation de dénomination is valid for 10 weeks (70 days) and cannot be extended; after expiry a new attestation may be requested free of charge. In the event of rejection on grounds of conflict with an existing RCS entry, trademark, or public-order-sensitive token: (1) obtain written grounds from the INPI or the Greffe; (2) re-file a revised name through the Guichet unique without penalty; (3) where administrative grounds are disputed, file a hierarchical or judicial appeal within two months under Articles R.421-1 et seq. of the Code des relations entre le public et l'administration; (4) where a trademark opposition underlies the refusal, bring proceedings before the Tribunal judiciaire (competent court) for a declaration of non-infringement or cancellation of the conflicting mark, or before the Tribunal de commerce on unfair-competition grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. A SAS may use a commercial domiciliation (virtual office) under Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-136-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce provided the domiciliation company is registered on the Domibis list and a written domiciliation contract is filed with the RCS. For an executive-search and headhunting agency (no inventory, no cash handling, no public reception required), a Domibis-registered virtual office is generally acceptable as the siège social. Alternatively, the président may use a personal residence for up to five years. No statutory rule imposes a physical office for this service activity, subject to GDPR and HR-file confidentiality arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 3–5% per year for a registered, low-risk executive-search and headhunting agency. Unannounced inspections remain legally possible by URSSAF (social-contribution control), by the inspection du travail (labor inspection, applicable only where staff are present), and by DGFiP in ordinary tax-audit cycles, but the probability is materially below cash-intensive or regulated financial sectors.

Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of foreign corporate and identity documents

UBO (bénéficiaire effectif) declaration preparation and filing support

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II – Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 (formation and operation of the SAS); Decree No. 2007-431 (Articles R. 224-1 et seq.); Code du travail Articles L. 5321-1 et seq. for recruitment licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce within the territorial jurisdiction of the company's registered office; application filed exclusively via the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation au Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, together with the executed Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs) and supporting annexes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS (freely fixed in the articles; €1 is lawful). In-cash subscriptions must be lodged in a French bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; at least 50% of cash contributions must be released at incorporation and the balance within five years. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up and valued in the articles.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty — taxpayer portal: www.impots.gouv.fr (espace professionnel and EDI). Business registration single-window: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs and indirect export controls: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — www.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SAS electronically through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the dossier to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the competent commercial court. 2. INSEE automatically attributes the statutory identification numbers: SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits). 3. The same filing automatically opens the corporate income tax (IS) and VAT files with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), which attributes the intra-Community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) in the format FR + 2-digit checksum + 9-digit SIREN. 4. Collect the Kbis extract as conclusive evidence of legal registration. 5. Activate the professional online tax account on impots.gouv.fr and subscribe to EDI (Échange de Données Informatisé) for mandatory electronic filing of IS and VAT returns. 6. Register a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) in view of the compulsory e-invoicing and e-reporting obligations from September 2027. 7. If goods are ever exported or imported, obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from the DGDDI; non-resident shareholders do not require French tax representation in the case of a French-established SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an operating French SAS is an opaque, French-tax-resident legal entity subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, article 205 CGI) on its worldwide profits. Profits are taxed at the standard rate of 25%, with a reduced rate of 15% applicable to the first €42,500 of taxable profit where annual turnover is below €10 million (article 219-IV-b CGI). France applies territoriality only to the participation-exemption regime (régime mère-fille) and to foreign permanent-establishment profits under treaty conditions; headhunting and executive-search fee income is fully within the scope of French entity-level taxation. No tax-exempt zone or statutory pass-through classification is available to an operating SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box or general pass-through election for business companies; an operating executive-search SAS cannot elect transparent taxation. Available statutory elections include: (i) option under article 239 ter CGI for an eligible pure-holding SAS (holding of securities or real estate only, without industrial or commercial activity) to be taxed as a société de personnes — not available to a headhunting agency; (ii) option under article 293 B CGI to waive the VAT franchise en base and become a full VAT taxpayer, valid for two years; (iii) VAT-group election (assujettissement unique) under article 256 C-II CGI for closely linked eligible entities established in France; (iv) French fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) under article 223 A CGI where the SAS holds at least 95% of a French subsidiary group; (v) no hybrid-mismatch elective relief exists — French transposition of ATAD statutorily denies deductions for hybrid payments and structures; (vi) automatic application of the reduced 15% small-business corporate rate and simplified filing regimes where statutory turnover thresholds are met.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for eligible small and medium enterprises; Research Tax Credit (CIR), Innovation Tax Credit (CII), territorial economic aid for repricing and innovation, and group tax integration (intégration fiscale) for qualifying French entities; the CICE has been abolished and replaced by structural payroll contribution reductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (liassez fiscale) with annexes 2050 to 2065, filed electronically via the EDI/EFI module of impots.gouv.fr; VAT and other indirect tax declarations may be submitted through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; VAT is filed quarterly or monthly depending on turnover.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline is 2 May (automatically extended to 3 May if 2 May is a weekend or public holiday).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification details, SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, legal form, address, quality of signatory and business activity description.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide French tax agent or branch registration details; ensure the French permanent establishment is identified and included in the corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement, operating receipts, executive-search retainer income, success fees, client reimbursements and all French-sourced operating revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a treaty allocation schedule; report only income attributable to the French permanent establishment of the non-resident headhunting group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, personnel costs, subcontractor fees, administrative overhead, travel and client-development charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length treatment to intra-group fees; deductibility is restricted if documentation is missing or the expense is unrelated to the French operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after adjustments; use of previously carried-forward losses, reductions of capital and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the French branch may be carried forward only against French-source profits; treaty-protected income is excluded from the computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimable tax credits and tax reductions, including CIR and CII, with supporting schedule attachments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit is calculated only for French permanent establishment research or qualifying activities; substantiate with the dedicated CERFA forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net taxable income or deficit submitted to the tax administration and serving as basis for the corporate income tax liquidation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with treaty permanent-establishment allocation and transfer-pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 0.5% per full month in arrears; 40% additional penalty for intentional omission, 80% for abusive manipulation or fictitious arrangements; daily surcharge of 0.2% per month for late payment; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 for individuals and EUR 1,000,000 for the corporation for tax evasion, with up to five years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119 bis of the French General Tax Code; 30% single flat withholding for non-resident individuals unless a tax treaty applies; residency-based exemptions apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home jurisdiction and submit it to the French paying agent or to the DGFiP before or at the time of payment. Form 5000/5001 may be used to claim treaty relief; refund claims follow the applicable treaty limitation period, generally two to three years from the dividend payment. The payer applies the treaty rate only when the TRC and ownership structure meet the DTA limitation-on-benefits provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax at 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU related companies under the Interest & Royalties Directive and to 0% or a reduced rate under most DTAs (e.g., 0% under France-Germany DTA with valid TRC). Interest: ordinary arm's-length interest paid to non-residents is exempt from French withholding tax, unless the beneficial owner is established in a non-cooperative jurisdiction, in which case a 75% withholding levy applies under Article 125 A CGI.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 group-wide annual turnover or balance-sheet total for mandatory Master File and Local File; EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue for Country-by-Country Reporting. French entities with turnover below these thresholds must still maintain simplified transfer-pricing documentation when intra-group transactions are present, as the tax administration may request it on audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, French case law and statutory rules enforce substance-over-form, abuse of law (abus de droit), abnormal acts of management (acte anormal de gestion), and the OECD principal purpose test. A shell entity lacking genuine activity, premises, personnel or decision-making functions may be disregarded, and income may be re-attributed under Articles 57 CGI and 155 A CGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful under-declaration of executive-search fees, submission of false annual returns, issuance or acceptance of fictitious retainer invoices, and concealment of a French permanent establishment by routing fees through an offshore shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 80% of the reassessed tax for fraudulent manipulation, 40% for bad-faith understatement; late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; criminal fine for tax evasion up to EUR 500,000 for individuals and EUR 1,000,000 for the corporation; imprisonment up to five years for responsible natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the entity's tax debts under Article 1745 CGI; travel bans, restriction on directly or indirectly managing legal entities, and imprisonment are available for serious fraud; DGFiP may seek civil restitution of taxes, penalties and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company & Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SAS as a French-registered shell with no local office, no operational decision-making, no substantive executive-search activity, and booking all fees to a foreign affiliate to claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization under Article 155 A CGI and abuse-of-law proceedings allowing the tax administration to disregard the shell; reassessment of French-source income over the full limitation period of six or seven years under abuse of law; 80% penalty for artificial arrangements; denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is possible where the shell is used to evade French tax; directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties, subject to travel bans and imprisonment for complicity in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging management fees, marketing fee allocations or intercompany success-fee commissions to or from a non-resident related party without an arm's-length benchmark or documentation, or with excessive profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment under Article 57 CGI with latent redistribution of taxable profits; late-payment interest; penalty for inadequate documentation equal to up to 5% of the reassessed amount if documents not provided within thirty days; up to 80% penalty if manipulation is demonstrated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve or conceal non-arm's-length arrangements may be held personally liable for the resulting tax adjustments under managed-company fault rules and also face criminal sanctions if the scheme is fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML & Money-Laundering Red Flags in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Circumventing the registered retainer wire payment system by accepting cash or unidentifiable Wise B2B transfers, obscuring the beneficial owner, or facilitating disguised fee-splitting transactions that conceal criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code (L. 561-1 et seq.), legal persons face fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for breach of AML/CTF obligations; natural persons face imprisonment up to ten years and fines up to EUR 750,000 for money-laundering; assets may be frozen and seized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML compliance failures; if they know or should know of laundering through retainer payments, they risk travel bans, criminal convictions, disgorgement of criminal assets and imprisonment.
